summary.intent: Deploy v0.25.0 to staging after release PR merge, then investigate and fix performance and auth issues discovered during smoke testing.
summary.outcome: v0.25.1 released (with Dockerfile and release-please config fixes), IPNS publish latency fixed via fire-and-forget DHT publish (PR #308), and the web app's fragmented HTTP client architecture consolidated onto a single api-client package (PR #309).

repo: Staging deployment is intentionally manual: merging a release PR creates the release tag, but staging deploy requires running the 'Tag Staging Release' workflow manually with the release tag as input.

release-please with multi-package config requires '${component}' in pull-request-title-pattern; omitting it causes release-please to abort on subsequent runs with 'untagged merged release PRs' even when all component tags exist.

The API is zero-knowledge by design — it never handles plaintext or performs encryption, so it genuinely has no workspace package dependencies. The stale COPY of packages/crypto in the Dockerfile was leftover from before this architecture solidified.
IPNS publish was awaiting DHT propagation via the someguy sidecar (10–30s) even though resolveRecord() always reads from the DB cache, making the wait pointless.

The web app had three separate HTTP client paths: (1) apps/web/src/api/custom-instance.ts (fetch, orval react-query mode), (2) apps/web/src/lib/api/client.ts (axios, used for login/vault init), (3) apps/web/src/lib/api/ipfs.ts (bare axios/fetch). None had consistent 401/refresh handling.

The orval react-query generated client (8,812 lines) was almost entirely unused — only 1 endpoint used the useXxx hooks. Everything else called raw generated functions identical to what @cipherbox/api-client already exports.
chore commit type does not trigger a release-please version bump; fix does. This matters when a CI fix needs a patch release.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate and return HTTP 503 with 'Your instance is loading' on first provisioning hit after inactivity — transient, not a real failure.

code.finding: DHT publish via delegated routing was awaited synchronously. Changed to fire-and-forget with trailing .catch() for error logging. The result variable previously could be set to 'delegated_error' but now stays 'success' since DB write is the source of truth.
Orval-generated fetch mutator with zero 401 handling — token expiry caused unrecoverable 401s. This file and the entire apps/web/src/api/ directory were deleted in the consolidation refactor.
Extended with refreshAccessToken callback, withCredentials support, and 401 response interceptor with shared-promise deduplication so concurrent requests don't each trigger a refresh.
Separate orval config generating react-query hooks directly into the web app using fetch client mode — duplicated the api-client package's generation. Deleted in consolidation.

pull-request-title-pattern was 'chore: release' without ${component}. In multi-package mode this prevents release-please from matching merged PRs back to components, causing it to abort all future runs.
Triggers on tags matching v*-staging* only — release tags like v0.25.0 do not trigger it. Staging deploy is always a manual step via the tag-staging.yml workflow.

workflow: When release-please gets stuck on 'untagged merged release PRs', manually creating the git tag and GitHub release unblocks subsequent runs without needing to rewrite history.
fix(ci) is the correct commit type for a broken CI/build fix that needs a patch release; chore(ci) would not trigger a version bump.
Codecov patch coverage checks fail on fire-and-forget error paths — need tests that make the async chain throw and assert the logger is called.
Investigating React Query hook usage before assuming the orval react-query mode is load-bearing can reveal dead generated code that can be cleanly removed.

friction: release-please silently aborted on v0.25.1 tag creation due to the missing ${component} pattern — the error message ('untagged merged release PRs') was misleading since the tags did exist.
Three separate HTTP client paths in the web app each needed independent auth fixes; the fragmentation had masked the token refresh gap for a long time.
The staging deploy not auto-triggering on release merge was initially mistaken for a release-please failure, requiring investigation before the actual (expected) behavior was recalled.
Codecov patch coverage failure surfaced after all review comments were resolved, requiring a separate test addition pass.
open_items: PR #307 (fix release-please pull-request-title-pattern with ${component}) needs merge before the next release cycle.
PR #308 (IPNS fire-and-forget DHT publish) needs merge, then Tag Staging Release re-run with v0.25.1 to complete the staging deployment.
PR #309 (consolidate web app onto @cipherbox/api-client) needs review — it removes ~8,800 lines of generated code and is the actual fix for the token refresh issue.
Verify future release-please runs work correctly after PR #307 merges — the root v0.25.0 PR was never properly matched to components, so the first post-fix release should be monitored.
Grafana provisioning job failure was not retried — may need a manual re-run or investigation into whether the dashboard state is stale.
